The fan shaped SRR absorber has an outer radius of 2.15 mm with line thickness and gaps of 0.15 mm.
Conventional rectangular SRR absorbers have a narrow fractional bandwidth of about 1% around 9.5 GHz.
The fan shaped SRR absorber achieves a fractional bandwidth of approximately 8% at 9.5 GHz and a second absorption band at 11.7 GHz.
The fan shaped SRR absorber maintains similar absorption performance for both co-polarized and cross-polarized incident waves.
The modified HIGP absorber uses a 2x2 unit cell with asymmetric slots (5.2 mm x 0.2 mm) cut into square patches of length 5.2 mm.
The modified HIGP absorber doubles the fractional bandwidth from 5.5% to 10%, with a 10 dB return loss bandwidth from 9.5 GHz to 10.5 GHz.
Both absorbers are implemented on FR4 substrate with εr=4.4, tan δ=0.02, and thickness 1.6 mm.
Full wave electromagnetic simulations were conducted using Ansoft software for both co-polarized and cross-polarized incident waves.
The fan shaped SRR absorber achieves reflection coefficients better than -15 dB at 9.5 GHz and better than -20 dB at 11.7 GHz.
The modified HIGP absorber achieves a minimum 10 dB return loss better than -20 dB at the center frequency of 10 GHz.
Surface mount resistors of 375 Ω are used in the modified HIGP absorber to connect patches to ground.
The fan shaped SRR geometry enhances parasitic effects enabling multi-band resonance.
The conventional rectangular SRR absorber fails to absorb cross-polarized waves effectively, showing near 0 dB reflection.
The modified HIGP absorber shows slightly different reflection responses for co-polarized and cross-polarized waves but maintains absorption below -15 dB.
The absorbers are designed to overcome the trade-off between absorber thickness and bandwidth.
The fan shaped SRR absorber increases bandwidth up to eight times compared to conventional SRR absorbers.
The modified HIGP absorber nearly doubles the bandwidth compared to conventional patch absorbers.
The absorbers are intended for radar cross section reduction and stealth technology applications.
Theoretical concepts are supported by equivalent circuit models of the SRR and metamaterial transmission line.
The study validates the absorbers' performance through simulated reflection coefficients for normal incidence.
